title: Thread surgery — surgical compression and selective excision notes
content:
Overview:

Quick personal notes about an interaction-level feature I'm calling 'Thread Surgery' — tools for programmatically and interactively pruning, compressing, and surgically excising parts of a conversation before sending context to the model. Goal: keep end-to-end latency and token cost low while preserving user intent and salient memory for future turns.

Motivation / problem statement:
- Long user sessions cause token bloat and rising per-request cost.
- Naive eviction can drop crucial context and break continuity.
- Need fine-grained tooling for: (1) compressing repetitive history, (2) removing sensitive or irrelevant spans, and (3) stitching a minimal "surgical" context that preserves salient facts and conversation state.

High-level idea:
- Provide a toolkit on the client/server side that can operate in three modes:
  1) Slice-and-compress: automatically condense long monologues and repeated assistant responses into short summaries (keep provenance).
  2) Excise: remove spans marked by policy (PII, off-topic, user-deleted) with audit-enabled replacement tokens.
  3) Stitch: re-order and tile short segments (anchors) with contextual glue to preserve intent and references.

User stories:
- As a product user, I want my assistant to forget a specific message I asked it to delete so later prompts don’t resurrect it. Acceptance: after excision, subsequent responses do not reference deleted content; audit log shows removal event.
- As an SRE, I want a configurable compression threshold so that sessions with >5k tokens get automatically condensed with single-line summaries for older turns. Acceptance: cost per session drops by target percentage in A/B test.
- As a developer, I want an API to request a "surgical context bundle" for a session id that returns a compressed context + provenance pointers. Acceptance: bundle size <= 25% of original tokens for long sessions and includes pointers to original turn ids.

Design sketches (implementation notes):
- Pipeline stages:
  1) Token scanner: compute TTL/age, relevance score (embedding similarity to current prompt), safety score.
  2) Tiler: choose candidate spans for compression/excision based on policy heuristics.
  3) Micro-summarizer: run short-summary model (cheap endpoint / distilled) to compress selected spans.
  4) Stitcher: assemble final context ordering anchors, summaries, and immediate previous turn.
  5) Audit layer: persist the surgery plan and diffs for rollback and compliance.

Relevance heuristics (rough):
- recency boost: linear decay over last N turns (configurable)
- mention-based: presence of named entities referenced in current prompt -> preserve
- role-change: if assistant provided an actionable step (code, plan) -> preserve full turn
- redundancy detection: identical or near-identical assistant messages -> compress to one anchor with frequency count

Safety / privacy considerations:
- Excise must produce cryptographic deletion token in audit log so Private deployments can honor legal delete requests.
- Summaries must be clearly labeled; if a user requests verbatim recall, the system should be able to surface provenance but not the excised verbatim in private setups.
- Provide policy hooks to mark turns uncompressible (legal hold, audit flag).

API surface (first draft):
- POST /v1/sessions/:id/surgery -> returns {bundle_id, token_count_before, token_count_after, operations[]} (ops are short strings like "compress turn 124 -> sum_124_v1", "excise turn 132")
- GET /v1/sessions/:id/bundles/:bundle_id -> returns compressed context as array of segments with metadata: {segment_text, origin_turn_ids, summary_model_version, excision_flag} (we store only pointers in the hosted product; for private deployments allow raw text return based on config)
- POST /v1/sessions/:id/surgery/preview -> returns diff view for UI preview (client can accept or modify plan)

UI sketch (client console):
- Inline "Surgery Preview" panel showing green (keep), yellow (compress), red (excise) banners per turn with short summary lines and toggles.
- Slider to control compression aggressiveness (conservative -> aggressive).
- Undo/rollback control for last N surgery operations.

Metrics / success criteria for experiments:
- Cost reduction: median tokens sent to model per session (target 30% reduction for sessions > 5k tokens within 4-week experiment).
- Latency delta: added preprocessing time < 60ms p50 for typical sessions; p95 < 300ms for long sessions (aim to keep overall end-to-end under SLOs).
- Quality retention: human eval on 200 sessions, measured by "contextual correctness" score with target >= 0.95 relative to baseline.
- Safety: false positive excision rate < 0.5% in manual review sample.

Experiment plan (MVP):
- Week 0–1: lightweight offline simulator: run thread-surgery heuristics against a snapshot of anonymized sessions (1000 sessions), measure token reduction, and flag problem cases.
- Week 2: small internal dogfood: enable preview API for internal team; collect feedback on UI and incorrect compressions.
- Week 3–4: A/B test on 5% of traffic for one client (opt-in) with conservative compression; monitor metrics.

Open questions / risks:
- How to define "salient" for multi-turn referential pronouns? Need anaphora-aware relevance scoring (maybe cheap embedding + coref heuristics).
- Proliferation of micro-summarizer models and model drift — need model-version tagging on summaries.
- Interaction with Dedicated/Private: audits and deletion semantics differ per deployment; add clear separation in API contract.
- Edge cases: induced hallucinations when summaries drop linking context (needs eval).

To-dos (short):
- [ ] Build offline simulator and run on anonymized session corpus (ask data infra for sample)
- [ ] Prototype micro-summarizer using a distilled 1B parameter model on hosted test cluster
- [ ] Draft API contract and raise initial RFC with devex + serving-runtime
- [ ] Wire an audit log shape with SRE/security for deletion proofs

Notes to self / heuristics I like:
- Prefer keep-first-last heuristic for long assistant monologues (first user ask + last assistant answer) and compress middle sequence.
- Compression budget per session (configurable) rather than per-turn cap — gives global view for tiler.
- Encourage explicit user opt-in for automatic surgery on privacy-sensitive apps.

References / inspiration:
- Prior convo compaction paper notes (Mira shared) — see confluence link in header.
- Internal work: session-eviction-playbook and compact-journey heuristics (cross-ref).

Closing thought: start conservative. The biggest win now is predictable unit economics and fewer surprise regressions; gradually move to more aggressive tiling once we have strong provenance and micro-eval gating.

-- Dante
